mat_wpc_19482.matterTitle: WP(C) 19482/2024 — Gopakumar v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Anr.
mat_wpc_19482.coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice A. Muhamed Mustaque & Hon'ble Mrs. Justice Shoba Annamma Eapen
mat_wpc_19482.hearingStage: Urgent Motion for Ad-Interim Injunction & Direction

issues.title: Jurisdictional Bar under Section 16(1) Telegraph Act
issues.question: Whether the licensee (KSEB) has unilateral statutory jurisdiction to proceed with stringing overhead lines across petitioner's yielding land once written objection under Section 16(1) has been registered, without referral to the District Magistrate?

issues.title: Breach of Natural Justice & Article 14/300A
issues.question: Whether Exhibit P-6 alignment notice passed behind the petitioner's back without spot inspection or personal hearing violates Audi Alteram Partem and proprietary protections under Article 300A?

issues.title: Statutory Duty to Minimize Damage (Section 10(d))
issues.question: Whether the respondents are bound to divert the alignment along the unobstructed public PWD road margin which runs 40 meters away, thereby causing 'least possible damage'?

precedents.caseName: Valsamma & Ors. v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Anr.
precedents.ratio: Licensee has no unbridled discretion to cut trees or draw lines through private land once an objection is raised. Referral to the District Magistrate under Section 16(1) is mandatory prior to commencement of works.
precedents.howToApply: Directly binding on Single Bench and Division Bench. Hand up certified true copy when countering Standing Counsel's contention on emergent grid needs.

precedents.caseName: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. v. Century Textiles & Industries Ltd.
precedents.ratio: Powers under Section 10 are subject to landowner's right to resist, which immediately triggers the adjudicatory jurisdiction of the District Magistrate under Section 16.
precedents.howToApply: Cite to show Supreme Court concord with Kerala High Court doctrine.

precedents.caseName: Bharat Plywood and Timber Products v. KSEB
precedents.ratio: Section 10(d) imposes an affirmative duty on electricity authorities to do the least possible damage to private lands.
precedents.howToApply: Use to argue for PWD road margin diversion.

benchInquiries.question: Counsel, why did your client wait 7 months between Exhibit P-6 order and filing this Article 226 petition?
benchInquiries.rebuttalAnswer: My Lord, the petitioner was diligently pursuing statutory representation Exhibit P-4 before the District Magistrate as commanded by Section 16(1). The delay is bona fide pursuit of administrative remedies, not contumacious laches. Moreover, physical entry was only threatened on 14-Aug-2024.
benchInquiries.supportingExhibits: Exhibit P-4 (Speed Post A/D) & Exhibit P-7 (Collectorate Diary Receipt)

benchInquiries.question: Is the line stringing already completed or are foundation towers erected?
benchInquiries.rebuttalAnswer: No, My Lord. Only wooden surveyor pegs were driven on 14-Aug-2024. No conductor stringing has occurred. An ad-interim stay preserves the absolute status quo with zero disruption to the statewide transmission network.

benchInquiries.question: Can an individual landowner stall a public infrastructure transmission project of state importance?
benchInquiries.rebuttalAnswer: My Lord, the petitioner is not stalling the grid. We are praying for route alignment along the unobstructed PWD road margin 40 meters west, or that the District Magistrate conduct the statutory hearing under Section 16(1) as required by the Division Bench in Valsamma.
benchInquiries.supportingExhibits: Exhibit P-5 (Re-survey Sketch & Alignment Comparison Map)

speakingNotes.heading: Opening & Impugned Memo
speakingNotes.content: May it please your Lordships: This Writ Petition challenges Exhibit P-6 unilateral alignment notice dated 04-03-2024. Petitioner is an agricultural smallholder in Aluva holding 28.5 Cents of registered rubber and fruit groves vide Exhibit P-1 title deed.

speakingNotes.heading: Statutory Violation of Section 16(1)
speakingNotes.content: On 14-Aug-2024, respondents entered the property without prior statutory notice. Petitioner immediately registered written objection Exhibit P-4. Section 16(1) of the Indian Telegraph Act is peremptory: the moment resistance is offered, licensee's executive power ceases until the District Magistrate orders entry.

speakingNotes.heading: Binding Division Bench Doctrine
speakingNotes.content: Handing up Valsamma v. KSEB [2024 (2) KHC 401 DB]. At Paragraph 18, their Lordships held that the licensee cannot sit in judgment of its own cause. Entry without Collector's order is illegal trespass.

speakingNotes.heading: Interim Ad-Interim Relief Prayer
speakingNotes.content: Praying for an interim order restraining tree felling and conductor stringing until Respondent No. 3 District Magistrate conducts hearing and renders formal decision on Exhibit P-4 objection.

questions.questionText: Before ordering the contractors to enter the property, did your department obtain an authorization order under Section 16(1) from the District Magistrate, Ernakulam?

questions.questionText: Is it not a fact that a 12-meter wide public PWD road runs parallel to the western boundary of the petitioner's property?
questions.objective: Prove feasible alternative alignment causing zero damage under Section 10(d)
questions.targetAdmission: Admits existence of public road margin
